questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop after a short distance to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Check the tire for wear.
Check the windshield wiper fluid level.
Check the tire air pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop after a short distance to make sure the lug nuts are still tight and secure.

questions.question: The body removes alcohol:

options.text: At a rate that changes based on how much alcohol is in the body.
At a steady rate, no matter how much alcohol is in the body.
Faster if the person drinks coffee.
Faster if the person stays awake.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a steady rate, no matter how much alcohol is in the body.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up, like drinking coffee or taking a cold shower. The only way to sober up is to wait for your body to process the alcohol naturally.

questions.question: When driving a charter bus, you should:

options.text: Explain how to use the TVs if the bus has them.
Not let passengers board until the scheduled departure time.
Let passengers board early to leave ahead of schedule.
Tell passengers to fill the back of the bus first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not let passengers board until the scheduled departure time.
questions.explanation: Do not let passengers board until the scheduled departure time. This helps prevent theft and damage to the bus.

questions.question: Baggage and cargo should be stored so that:

options.text: Riders can exit through any door or window in an emergency.
Items block an exit if another exit is available.
Items partially cover a door since they can be moved.
Cargo can be removed quickly in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders can exit through any door or window in an emergency.
questions.explanation: Store all baggage and cargo so the driver can move freely, riders can exit through any door or window in an emergency, and items cannot fall and hurt riders.

questions.question: Bent lock rings:

options.text: Are acceptable.
Are safe in dry weather.
Are dangerous.
Help tires last longer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are dangerous.
questions.explanation: Bent, cracked, or mismatched lock rings are dangerous and must not be used.

questions.question: You can tell a vehicle has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) by:

options.text: A sticker on the control panel.
A yellow warning light on the dashboard.
The letters "ABS" printed on the brake pedal.
A metal plate inside the driver's door.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow warning light on the dashboard.
questions.explanation: A vehicle with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) will have a yellow ABS warning light on the dashboard.

questions.question: When driving a school bus, your four-way flashers should:

options.text: Be turned on before crossing railroad tracks.
Never be used.
Only be used after crossing railroad tracks.
Only be used near railroad tracks if a train is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be turned on before crossing railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way flashers while approaching and crossing railroad tracks. Turn them off once the entire bus has cleared the tracks.

questions.question: When turning left with two left turn lanes available, which lane should you use?

options.text: The left lane
The right lane
Either lane
Large vehicles should not turn where there are two left turn lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need extra room to make left turns. When two left turn lanes are available, use the right lane to start your turn.

questions.question: When inspecting springs, do all of the following except:

options.text: Look for missing leaf springs.
Look for broken coil springs.
Check that torsion springs are not damaged.
Glue cracked leaf springs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glue cracked leaf springs.
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, look for missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs. Check for broken or bent coil springs. For vehicles with torsion bars or other suspension parts, make sure they are not damaged and are mounted securely. Do not glue springs.

questions.question: Suspension system problems may include all of the following except:

options.text: Cracked or broken spring hangers.
Missing or broken leaf springs.
Leaking shock absorbers.
Cracked lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cracked lights.
questions.explanation: Check your suspension system for cracked or broken spring hangers, missing or broken leaves, and leaking shock absorbers. Get these problems fixed right away.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Set the parking brake.
Set the air brakes.
Not set any brake.
Disconnect the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Set the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always set the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: When traction is poor, a driver should accelerate slowly:

options.text: Because slow acceleration is always best.
So they keep control of their vehicle.
So they don't go faster than the vehicle ahead.
To be the last vehicle through an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: So they keep control of their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerating too quickly on slippery roads can cause you to lose control. When traction is poor, accelerate smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: Before driving a bus, you should make sure it is safe by:

options.text: Reading the inspection report from the previous driver.
Kicking the tires.
Asking your supervisor if the bus seems safe.
Asking passengers if they feel comfortable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reading the inspection report from the previous driver.
questions.explanation: Always inspect a bus before driving it. Check the inspection report from the previous driver. Only drive the bus if all defects have been fixed or marked as not needing repair.

questions.question: If a tire rim is damaged, it should be:

options.text: Left on the vehicle.
Welded to fix the damage.
Replaced.
Put on the axle farthest from the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Replaced.
questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded are not safe to use.

questions.question: When taking the basic vehicle control skills test:

options.text: Points are taken away for each pull-up.
A driver can do three pull-ups per maneuver.
A pull-up earns points only if the driver gets out before pulling up.
Only too many pull-ups count as errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only too many pull-ups count as errors.
questions.explanation: During the basic vehicle control skills test, one pull-up is allowed without penalty. However, too many pull-ups will count as errors.

questions.question: Carry-on bags should be placed:

options.text: In front of the back door.
In front of the front door.
Where all emergency exits can be reached.
On top of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where all emergency exits can be reached.
questions.explanation: Do not block doorways or aisles with luggage. All bags must be placed so passengers can exit from any door or window in an emergency.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Can damage a vehicle.
Is needed to warm up the engine.
Improves gas mileage.
Should be done on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can damage a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration causes mechanical damage.

questions.question: When driving:

options.text: Always drive at the posted speed limit.
Always drive slightly below the posted speed limit.
Change your speed based on road and weather conditions.
Drive as fast as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your speed based on road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast is a major cause of serious crashes. You must adjust your speed to match current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Radial and bias-ply tires:

options.text: Can be used together on all axles.
Can be used together, but only on the rear axle.
Should not be used together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used together.
questions.explanation: When inspecting your vehicle, make sure radial and bias-ply tires are not mixed on the same vehicle.

questions.question: What are placards?

options.text: Warning signs on a vehicle that show what cargo hazards are being carried
A type of tire used in snow
Records kept inside the vehicle
Books for tracking mileage

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs on a vehicle that show what cargo hazards are being carried
questions.explanation: Placards are diamond-shaped warning signs placed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They identify the specific type of hazard being transported.
